title: A return percentage of what?
hook: Two stated cases: explore the recipient pot as the return denominator.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How the recipient pot as the return denominator affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Sender, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare the recipient pot as the return denominator in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: A toy sender has 10, sends 5, which is multiplied by 3; the recipient returns fraction 0.37 of that pot. What does the sender finish with?

claims.text: Sending and returning are two decisions. A multiplier creates surplus, but the sender’s payoff also depends on the return rule. This comparison isolates the recipient pot as the return denominator.

recall.question: A toy sender has 11, sends 5, which is multiplied by 3; the recipient returns fraction 0.37 of that pot. What does the sender finish with?
recall.why: The same explicit rule gives Sender 11.55 for the changed inputs. This is a new numerical case.
